body: Closing as superseded by the current typed MintQuote.method field and BOLT11, BOLT12, and on-chain quote subtypes. The remaining request for plugin-specific metadata will be scoped and tracked in a separate superseding issue; this closure does not claim arbitrary plugin metadata is implemented.

Closing as superseded by the accepted decisions to keep public custom repository adapters with scoped compatibility (ADR-0013) and to start every Coco Session through Manager.create/initializeCoco (ADR-0017). The opaque-storage and manual-construction design in this specification is no longer planned. The separate managed-SQLite requirements remain tracked in #530.

Closing as delivered. PR #613 added recovery for interrupted Send reclaims, and Melt recovery also handles legacy rolling_back records using fresh nonpayment evidence. Recovery preserves ambiguous outcomes rather than force-failing or releasing resources without positive evidence. Legacy Sends whose token proofs are spent but which have no persisted reclaim request can remain unresolved and may require seed Restore; this closure does not promise automatic recovery for every historical record.

Closing as completed. The work landed across #518, #550, and #561: polling preserves complete Melt Quote responses, recovery persists canonical observations before applying outcomes, and background settlement advances from stored evidence without an unconditional refetch. Agreed clarification of the original acceptance criteria: omitted change on an otherwise complete PAID response means zero change; partial/state-only notifications are outside the supported protocol contract and are ignored rather than enriched through another request. Incomplete previously stored settlement evidence still cannot authorize settlement as zero change. Fresh UNPAID confirmation before releasing operation-owned inputs remains an intentional safety check.

Closing as not planned. #607 addressed Send completion while subscription acquisition is pending. A narrower race remains when completion happens during the preceding trust lookup, before watch ownership is registered: a subscription can be installed after the Send finalizes and remain until watcher shutdown. The controlled reproduction showed unnecessary subscription retention, with the Send finalized correctly; no fund loss, incorrect balance, or meaningful performance degradation was demonstrated. We accept this low-impact cleanup gap rather than track a dedicated fix. It can be addressed opportunistically during future watcher work.

Closing as not planned. #607 and #631 addressed untrust during pending subscription acquisition and subsequent reacquisition. A narrower race remains when the mint becomes untrusted during the preceding trust lookup: its delayed true result can allow a subscription to be installed afterward. A controlled reproduction demonstrated subscription retention until watcher shutdown, but no financial impact or meaningful performance degradation was demonstrated. As with #562, we accept this low-impact cleanup gap rather than track a dedicated fix; it can be addressed opportunistically during future watcher work.

Re @mubarak23's question: yes, there is a second case, and it affects a receiver who *does* hold the original key. It happens when the secret has a `locktime` but **no `refund` tag**.

In `getReceiveSigningKeys` (main 3e5282e), `if (expired && refundKeys === undefined) return [];`. `prepareProofsForReceiving` then sends the proof with `witness: undefined`. If the wallet clock is ahead of the mint's and the wallet has passed `locktime` while the mint has not, the mint still requires the main-key signature, so it rejects a proof the receiver could have signed.

I checked this by calling `getReceiveSigningKeys` directly, with `locktime = L` and the main and refund keys generated from fixed test seeds:

| secret | wallet `now` | signing keys |
|---|---|---|
| locktime + refund | L − 60 | MAIN |
| locktime + refund | L + 60 | MAIN, REFUND |
| locktime, no refund | L − 60 | MAIN |
| locktime, no refund | L + 60 | `[]` (no witness) |
| locktime, no refund | L | MAIN |

With a refund tag, original keys come first, as you read. Skew only bites there when the receiver holds just the refund key (sender reclaiming), or in the mirror case where the wallet is *behind* the mint: the refund path isn't offered yet, and `signWithKeys` throws "Key pair not found" even though the mint would accept the refund signature.

The no-refund case has a mirror too. A wallet behind the mint, without the main key, tries MAIN, throws, and refuses a proof the mint already treats as anyone-can-spend.

One possible change: when the wallet holds a main key, always sign with it, even after `locktime` with no refund tag. If mints ignore an unneeded witness on an unlocked proof (I have not checked cdk or nutshell on this), that removes the skew dependency for the common receiver. The empty-witness path would then only be used when the wallet holds none of the keys.

Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review" or "@codex security review". Codex reacts with 👀 while any review is running, comments if it has suggestions, and reacts with 👍 once all reviews finish with no findings.
